html:
Anawrahta was the king who founded the Pagan Empire, the first state to unite the Irrawaddy valley of what is now Myanmar. He ruled from 1044 until his death in 1077, and Burmese history that can be checked begins with his reign.

He took a small kingdom in the dry zone of Upper Burma and made it strong by building irrigation works in the rice lands of Kyaukse. Then he expanded in all directions. His most famous campaign, in 1057, took Thaton, a Mon kingdom in the south, and brought its monks, scholars, craftsmen and Pali scriptures to Pagan.

With the monk Shin Arahan he made Theravada Buddhism the main faith of his realm, in place of older local cults and other Buddhist schools. He began the building of temples and stupas such as the Shwezigon Pagoda that would fill the plain of Pagan with thousands of monuments. Burmese call him the father of their nation. His empire lasted until Mongol attacks in the late 1200s.
